A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same detached-Jacobian research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material relocated or reformatted in v3.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments, singular-vector and layer analyses, and steering outcomes in Figures 3–6, Table 4 and the appendix.

after.justification: V3 retains original reconstruction and steering results and adds double-precision validation, a 100-phrase comparative analysis and additional model results.

M1.justification: The core gradient detachments, Jacobian reconstruction and steering equation remain unchanged. V3 Section 3.1 adds an approximate Lanczos procedure implemented in JAX to compute leading singular vectors without forming the full Jacobian, extending the computational procedure.

E1.justification: V3 broadens the bridge/geography-centered examples to varied English phrases involving actions, objects and abstract concepts in Section 3.4 and Appendix A.5. The underlying next-token task remains unchanged; multilingual decoded tokens do not establish evaluation on multilingual input datasets.

E2.justification: The conventional Jacobian remains the reconstruction baseline, and normal unsteered responses remain the steering control. Additional model analyses apply the same proposed method to different models. Newly cited sparse-autoencoder and probing approaches are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: V3 adds float64 reconstruction checks with absolute and relative allclose tolerances of 10^-13, replacing the standard-deviation error ratio with a norm ratio. It introduces a 100-phrase evaluation and Lanczos tests at longer sequence lengths. Reported configurations also change; the layer tables relabel Qwen 3 8B as 14B despite matching entries, which does not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 Section 3.4, Figure 3 and Appendix A.5 add systematic comparisons across 100 phrases, examining rank distributions, shared dominant directions, abstract versus concrete semantics, multilingual tokens and morphological fragments. Figure A5 adds comparative cases. The earlier layerwise analysis and steering demonstrations are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V3 introduces descriptive statistical aggregation: Figure 3 reports empirical stable-rank distributions and token-position means across 100 phrases, while Section 3.4 reports category frequencies. Neither version supplies repeated-seed results, confidence intervals or significance tests; these additions characterize variation across inputs rather than repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: V3 adds approximately 10^-15 float64 reconstruction errors, 100-phrase rank and semantic findings, and Phi 4 Mini, Ministral and OLMo2 plots previously only referenced externally. These are new or replaced results under changed settings, not same-setting gains over v1's float32/float16 errors. Appendix layer tables omit later-token columns, while steering outputs and the older cross-family SVD plots remain.

T1.justification: Section 2.3.2 replaces the explicit SwiGLU gated-product derivation in Equations 7–10 with a beta-parameterized Swish derivation. The normalization and attention derivations, reconstruction identity, stable-rank definition, steering equation and appendix GELU derivation retain their substance. No substantial new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The core claims of input-specific linear equivalence, low-dimensional structure and interpretable singular vectors remain. V3 sharpens the reconstruction claim to below 10^-13 at double precision and introduces Lanczos-based scalability in the conclusion. Its pointwise framing clarifies a restriction already stated in v1 rather than establishing a fundamentally different equivalence claim.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantial interpretations of dominant vectors as grammatical scaffolding, Llama's abstract semantics, Qwen's cross-lingual representations and morphological word construction. It also interprets steering as validation of semantic representations and discusses the precision–scalability tradeoff. The restriction to the particular input where the Jacobian was computed already appears in v1.

D1.justification: V3 adds runtime and GPU-memory examples, JAX/Lanczos implementation information, singular-vector truncation settings and explicit cosine-similarity decoding details. Access instructions also change: the abstract supplies a different repository address, while Appendix A.1 says code is supplied as a zip and will be published on GitHub, leaving an internal inconsistency.

R1.justification: V3 adds references on linear probes, the polytope perspective, mechanistic interpretability, normalization and newer sparse autoencoders, while dropping He and Hofmann. It expands the comparison with sparse-autoencoder training requirements and connects steering to Golden Gate Claude. The principal positioning relative to Elhage, Mohan and Kadkhodaie remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially revised, with systematic replacement of locally linear terminology by equivalent or pointwise linear terminology. The introductory generation illustration and cross-family discussion move into the appendix, and the main narrative is reorganized around the new comparative analysis.

P2.justification: V3 changes the document from two columns to one, combines the architecture diagram with a reconstruction plot, adds rank histograms and comparative figures, and reorganizes supplementary plots. Layer tables are redesigned around three input-token columns instead of seven or eight. Several earlier figures are retained through relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens validation through double-precision reconstruction checks and the 100-phrase analysis, extending v1's heavily bridge-centered evidence. Clearer pointwise terminology and more readable tables also help. Gains are tempered by omitted table data and overstated semantic interpretations. Section 3.4 also contradicts Figure 3: Llama's beginning-of-text mean rank, 1.0585, exceeds the first text token's 1.0230, contrary to the prose. These issues limit, but do not erase, the improvement.
